extracted.intended_audience: aspiring writers, students of literature/aesthetics, and culturally-minded readers seeking guidance on style and the cultivation of sensibility
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance on cultivating sensuous, cultured prose and a life of aesthetic insight — covering attention to sensation, refining perceptual faculties, language and style, moral restraint, and disciplined study. Useful for writers and critics aiming to render present experience vividly and memorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict attentiveness / self-consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject a careless, half-conscious 'use-and-wont' reception of experience; cultivate a strenuous self-consciousness and loyalty to cool and candid reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes scorn for careless reception of our experience and prescribes 'strict attentiveness of mind' as almost a religious duty; practice precepts towards strenuous self-awareness in all we think and do to avoid being misled by uncorrected sensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceive flux yet discern intelligible harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that visible things are in perpetual change, but seek the continuance of orderly intelligible relationships — a harmony amid mutation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heraclitean insight: perceive in the 'perpetual flux' of things an underlying principle of intelligible relationships (likened to the harmony of musical notes), rather than despairing at change; this perception of order amid motion is a mark of philosophic sanity and useful to the artist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on direct sensation and the present moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit knowledge and artistic attention to what is immediately felt; make the present the primary field of life and art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Cyrenaic/Epicurean practical conclusion: 'the present' alone can be relied upon — 'America is here and now' — so cultivate attachment to immediate phenomena of the senses, which 'never deceive us about themselves', and arrange life and art to 'improve the present with an absolutely disengaged mind.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine perceptual instruments (insight through culture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Education's aim is to develop and refine inward and outward intuition — the capacities of reception — so that experience may be perceived with increasing subtlety and fullness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that the right education is not transmission of abstract truths but an art: 'refining all the instruments of inward and outward intuition'; music and the finer arts play a central role in cultivating exquisite appreciation and making the vision of experience 'beatific'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate metaphysical thought into ethical/sentimental practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert abstract metaphysical doctrines into precepts that guide feeling and conduct, so speculative ideas become practical and life-enhancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aristippus's example shows how metaphysical 'shadows' become stimulative when rendered as sentiments or precepts: turn abstract doctrine into 'precepts of grace, and delicate wisdom' rather than allowing it to produce enervating nihilism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value fulness of life, not crude hedonism
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek a fullness of life characterized by energy, variety, choice of experiences (including noble pain), rather than reducing life to mere sensual indulgence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish refined 'fulness of life' and 'insight' from mere 'hedonism' — appreciating pleasures of art, study, moral endeavour and love; the 'new Cyrenaicism' takes the criterion of value from heroic, impassioned, and ideal forms of life, not from crude appetite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words should be things — transparency of language
rubrics_metrics.description: Language must transparently convey the writer's apprehension, emotion, and mood; words ought to function as tangible things that carry the reader into the experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases like 'words should be indeed things' and 'the phrase, valuable in exact proportion to the transparency with which it conveyed to others the apprehension' underline that genuine style follows from a virile apprehension of the true nature of things and that language should make that apprehension palpable to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine style requires self-understanding first
rubrics_metrics.description: True style depends on a prior sincere understanding of one's own impressions and character; self-knowledge is the first condition of authentic expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text states 'a true understanding of one’s self being ever the first condition of genuine style' — writers should cultivate inward clarity so that language naturally follows and transparently expresses their vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language qualities: delicate, measured, firm, and finished
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for language that is delicate and measured (e.g., Attic phrase), with firmness of outline and a 'cleanly finished structure' — model sentences on scrupulous thought and workmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage praises 'language delicate and measured', the 'delicate Attic phrase', and a 'touch of the worker in metal' in style; the 'happy phrase or sentence' should be modelled upon a finished structure achieved by erasure and careful crafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose with memory and arresting detail in mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose so that moments are arresting and memorable; aim to 'imprison' the perfume of the flowers — to create fragments of perfect expression that outlast their moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrator notes a desire to 'arrest, for others also, certain clauses of experience' and that one's 'main concern was its impression for the memory' — craft images and phrases that will remain vivid in recollection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid metaphysical idols and abstractions that distort perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Rid the mind of false appearances and preconceived notions (idola) that misrepresent experience; minimize speculative metaphysics in favour of concrete observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advice to 'be absolutely virgin towards such experience' and to neutralise the distorting influence of metaphysical systems echoes Baconian idola: spend little time on abstruse metaphysic and return to the world of concrete impressions as the primary source for art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical restraint: do not add to people's unhappiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain moral responsibility in life and art — avoid causing or increasing the suffering of others through one's conduct or expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrator records a 'determination... to add nothing, not so much as a transient sigh, to the great total of men’s unhappiness' — aesthetic pursuits should be balanced by conscience and a sense of social responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry, discipline, and rigorous revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustain a life of industrious study under healthy rule, employing rigorous erasure and correction in one's work; celebrate labour and discipline as sources of stylistic firmness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text prescribes 'a life of industry, of industrious study, only possible through healthy rule' and notes that the 'happy phrase' is 'modelled upon a cleanly finished structure of scrupulous thought' — implying systematic revision and disciplined practice are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorician/critic as interpreter and public teacher
rubrics_metrics.description: See the role of the rhetorician or critic as the eloquent interpreter of art and thought for others — a public lecturer or essayist who communicates appreciation and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage describes the rhetorician's work as largely criticism: 'the eloquent and effective interpreter... of what understanding himself had come by' and points to the public lecturer/essayist model as a legitimate vocational aim for the cultured writer.
